page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DADSv5 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It is equipped with 3686 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage options, while containing no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core tests placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Cryptographic capabilities are also highly efficient, as demonstrated by a top-tier rating in PassMark CPU encryption tests, aided by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. Memory performance is robust, with PassMark memory scores and small-block cached read bandwidth both ranking in the top 25%. However, large-block uncached memory read and write speeds, along with single-threaded compression and text processing tasks, register in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the D96ads_v5 offers a balanced ratio of compute to memory alongside a substantial local storage allocation, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high parallel processing capacity without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The server is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, software compilation, and large-scale web serving.
